overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights a dominant viewer preference for extreme space scenarios, cosmic what-if scenarios, and bizarre planetary extremes. Content published within the last 7 days (e.g., planetary exploration, exotic materials, and unusual cosmic conditions) vastly outperforms older psychology and standard biological facts in views-per-day, likes-per-view, and engagement. Specifically, high-performing videos feature high-stakes speculative hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with vivid, tactile imagery.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views), and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views) are driving the highest views-per-day and like ratios among recent uploads.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes space what-if scenarios and bizarre planetary phenomenons, framing the premise around surreal survival or extreme physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring vivid sensory elements like 'Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,027 views) and 'Rains Supersonic Rubies' (723 views) capture immediate attention and achieve strong engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Use visual-first, sensory-rich adjectives (e.g., boiling, invisible, crystalline, pitch-black) in the opening three seconds to instantly build a mental picture.

weak_patterns.pattern: Generic Psychological Tricks & Standard Human Biology Facts
weak_patterns.evidence: Older or less dynamic topics such as 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) exhibit extremely low velocity and poor engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard self-help psychology facts unless they can be tied to a shocking, highly counterintuitive historical or high-tech anomaly.

weak_patterns.pattern: Low-Stakes Animal Trivia Without Environmental Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Straightforward animal facts like 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' or standard octopus trivia show plateaued growth compared to cosmic extremes.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal and nature content toward cinematic survival or extreme habitat extremes rather than simple listicle facts.

next_video.concept: Exploring the bizarre physics of a rogue planet hurtling through interstellar space with no star to orbit, completely frozen in perpetual darkness.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a direct sensory shock: 'What happens when a wandering planet gets ejected from its solar system and freezes down to absolute zero?'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite being colder than deep space, its core remains glowing hot from radioactive decay, creating an underground liquid ocean beneath miles of ice.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high performance of 'What If' space scenarios and extreme planetary environments ('Planet of Burning Ice', 'Darker Than Coal') which show maximum traction.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not use black holes, diamond planets, gas giants, or the specific planets mentioned in the data history (Venus, TrES-2b).
Must focus on a rogue interstellar planet concept not previously covered.

experiment: Test a 21-second runtime utilizing a direct 'What If' speculative hook about an unknown interstellar phenomenon, comparing its 48-hour velocity against standard fact-based space titles.
